fixtures.label: Flat per-unit levy on a zero-priced component
fixtures.description: The only fixture carrying a `flat` (per-unit) TAX, and the reason the `hide_zero_priced_components` param can work on an invoice at all. An invoice line has NO `zero_priced` field — `projectOrderItemToInvoiceItem` does not carry it — so the param's predicate is `price.base_cents === 0 && componentDepth > 0`, checked on the stored amount rather than on the order's flag. This document is what proves that predicate finds the right row: 10 cases of water carry a zero-priced `Bottled Water ( /bottle )` child at 24 bottles each, and the Water Bottle Tax bills 240 x $0.05 = $12.00 against a $0.00 subtotal, beside 10.5% Chicago Sales Tax on the $390.00 parent. The flat tax arm reads QUANTITY and ignores subtotal, so it is the one branch that can put real money on a line whose Unit Price and Subtotal are both $0.00 — which is what the em-dash cell rule exists for: an em-dash says the value was computed and is nothing, where a blank would read as missing data. With the param ON the row hides and its $12.00 must roll onto the parent (Tax $40.95 -> $52.95, Total $430.95 -> $442.95) while #totals still reads $442.95, so the grid reconciles with its own footer instead of losing the money. It is also the family's only COMPONENT fixture: the child sits at path depth 5 under a three-level `[order, destination, group]` hierarchy and resolves to component depth 1, which is what proves `componentDepth` counts line-item ancestors rather than subtracting a fixed number of divider levels. Renders 7 columns. Captured from prod invoice 2390, the invoice for order 1004 — the same order behind the quote family's `taxed-zero-priced-component`, so the two families can be compared on one document. Measured 2026-08-26, order 1004 is still the only one of 997 prod orders carrying a flat tax, so if this fixture is dropped do not assume a replacement is available.

fixtures.label: Partly paid — a real Amount Due
fixtures.description: The only fixture with a NON-ZERO Amount Due, and therefore the only one where the settlement block says something a quote never can. $196.25 paid against $306.50, leaving $110.25 outstanding, at status `part_paid`. Settlement is the invoice's whole reason for existing as a separate family, and it is unreachable in detail: `Invoice.payments[]` was deleted 2026-08-03 and `InvoiceSchema` is a `z.strictObject`, so it cannot come back — the per-settlement journal is a separate `settlements` collection and a template only ever receives `it.doc`. So the document reports ROLLUPS, and this fixture is what pins them rendering correctly. It exercises the two rows that always print (Amount Paid, Amount Due) while leaving Credits Applied ABSENT, which is the other half of the rule: a credits row is omitted entirely at zero, because "$0.00 credited" states an absence as if it were a fact. Pair it with `credits-applied`, which covers the arm where it does print; a template that hard-coded the row would pass on that one alone. Renders 7 columns — tax on, no rental so no Duration, no discount. Captured from prod invoice 2364.

fixtures.label: Credits applied — all three settlement rows
fixtures.description: The only fixture that renders the Credits Applied row, and the only one where all three settlement rows carry a non-zero figure: $399.00 paid, $40.90 credited, against a $439.90 total. `totals.amount_credited_cents` is a bare `.optional()` with NO schema default, so most invoices simply do not have it and every read needs `?? 0` — this is the document that proves the row appears when the field is present, where `part-paid` proves it stays absent when it is not. Those two fixtures are a pair and neither substitutes for the other: one covers the conditional being true, the other covers it being false, and a template that hard-coded the row would pass on this one alone. Also worth knowing when reading a diff: Amount Due is $0.00 here while the invoice is fully settled, so this is the fixture that shows a zero Amount Due still printing — grand totals are deliberately exempt from the blank-at-zero rule, because a settled balance of zero is a fact about the invoice rather than an absent value. Captured from prod invoice 1252.

fixtures.label: 6-column floor, and a fee that must not be a row
fixtures.description: Two jobs no other fixture does. First, the 6-COLUMN FLOOR: one untaxed service line, no rental anywhere and no discount, so every conditional column in the items grid is off and the header is exactly Item Description / Type / Qty / Unit Price / Subtotal / Total. It is also therefore the only fixture where `hasCollection` is false — that is derived from `hasRentals`, because nothing on a sale or a service is ever collected — so it is what proves the destinations block collapses its return leg rather than printing headed empty columns. Second, and the reason it was chosen over any other untaxed invoice: it carries a `transaction_fee` ITEM alongside the service line. A transaction fee is stored in `items[]` but is NOT a line of the invoice — it is priced FROM the document, and `totals.transaction_fees` is DERIVED from these very items, so rendering both puts the same money on the page twice and a customer reads it as being charged twice. This fixture is what pins the suppression: the fee must appear in the totals block and NOT in the items grid. Nothing else in the set carries one. Consequence worth knowing when reading its output: the Total column does not sum to `totals.total_cents`, because the fee is added after the line items — that is the ordinary shape, not a defect. Captured from prod invoice 2353, which bills order 977 — the same order behind the quote family's `service-untaxed`, so the 6-column floor can be compared across both families on one document.

fixtures.label: 9-column ceiling, single view
fixtures.description: The 9-COLUMN CEILING — Duration, Discount and Tax all on at once, which is the widest grid the template can emit and therefore the one that decides whether the money columns still fit under `table-layout: fixed`. Two rentals in one group with a $4.00 discount and a percent tax, on a $50.62 invoice: deliberately the smallest carrier of the shape available, so the whole grid is readable in a single view and a column-width regression is obvious rather than buried. Keep it small — its job is the column combination and nothing else, so do not enrich it with content. The 9-column count is also what makes it the fixture that exercises `--block-3-fraction` at its odd-count value: `addressBoundary = floor((9-1)/2) = 4` of 8 address sub-columns, an exact half, where the even counts land off-centre. Alongside `service-untaxed-fee` at 6 columns and `zero-priced-flat-tax` at 7, this pins the range the shared items-grid partial has to survive — the same 6-to-9 span the quote family covers, rendered from the same partial. Captured from prod invoice 1902.

fixtures.label: Foreign billing address
fixtures.description: The only fixture whose `organization.billing_address.country_name` is not `United States` — a Canadian address — and therefore the only one that renders the country line in `#bill-to` at all. Every other fixture bills to a US address, so without this the conditional is dead in every golden and a green run says nothing about it. That is not a hypothetical failure mode: on the quote family this same country line, and the flat-tax totals row, were both dead branches that passed every run until a fixture reached them. Deliberately the SMALLEST carrier available at $146.52, so the golden diff shows the address block and little else. Its 8-column Duration + Tax grid is incidental rather than its job — but it is nonetheless the family's ONLY carrier of that shape, which is the commonest thing production writes, so do not delete it as a near-duplicate of the address coverage: `rental-discount-untaxed` holds the other 8-column shape (Duration + Discount) and neither substitutes. Measured 2026-08-26 by rendering the set. KNOWN ARTIFACT, do not "repair" the baseline: the postcode renders as `Sample t` rather than a masked postcode, because `applyPii`'s postcode branch is guarded on US ZIP (`/^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$/`) and a Canadian code falls through every branch to the generic filler. Tracked as api-cloudrun#627; when it lands, re-capture this fixture and re-bless its golden together. The country line itself, which is what the fixture is for, renders correctly. Captured from prod invoice 1918.

fixtures.label: Discount with no Tax column beside it
fixtures.description: 8 columns via Duration + Discount with Tax OFF — the only fixture that lays a Discount column out with no Tax column next to it, because `totals.taxes` is empty. That combination matters because the two conditional columns are adjacent in the header and a mistake in one arm reads as a mistake in the other: with Tax present, a Discount bug is easy to mis-attribute. Three rentals in one group with a $12.00 discount against a $48.00 total, so the discount is a quarter of the invoice and any rounding error in the Discount cell is visible at a glance rather than lost in a large figure. It is also the only fixture that renders the `Subtotal after Discount` row in the totals block, which only appears when `totals.discount_amount_cents > 0`. The family's OTHER 8-column shape is Duration + Tax with Discount off, and that is `billing-foreign-country` — measured, not assumed: rendered 2026-08-26, this fixture emits 8 columns and so does that one, while `part-paid` emits 7 (it has tax but no rental, so no Duration). A reader who sees only the column count will take one of the two 8-column fixtures for a duplicate of the other; they are not, and neither substitutes. Captured from prod invoice 1996.
